key_insight: Local flow splitting and merging in disordered pore networks produces Gamma-distributed pore-body flow rates, which in turn determine throat flow statistics.
engineering_relevance: The model offers a low-parameter way to predict flow heterogeneity in porous media from simple geometry, useful for designing and analyzing filters, catalysts, and subsurface flows.
method: Build a pore-network model for steady Stokes flow in 2D disordered arrays of circular obstacles
Capture local flow correlations from splitting and merging at pore junctions
Link the Gamma distribution parameter to the coefficient of variation of pore-throat widths
evidence_signal: The theory matches computational fluid dynamics simulations closely and outperforms prior mean-field models that ignore local flow-rate correlations.
watch_item: The framework is developed for steady Stokes flow in two-dimensional disordered porous media, so extension to inertial, transient, or fully 3D settings may require new validation.
paper_title: Topological origin of flow distributions in disordered porous media
